texts: An 8-year-old patient with a z-score over 3 is not, by that alone, an indication for surgery: E.
In children the absolute size, the rate of growth and the type of disorder matter more than a moderate z-score.
Indications include a root of about 5 cm in Marfan syndrome (less in Loeys-Dietz), rapid growth, progressive aortic insufficiency and a family history of premature dissection.
In the picture, only the 8-year-old with a z-score of 3 goes back to play.
Memory hook: a z of three sends the child back to the swings.
